questions.q: State the ICMR 2020 Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) for energy (kcal/day) and protein (g/day) for a 10-year-old boy and a 10-year-old girl, and explain why they differ.
questions.a: ICMR 2020 RDA for 10-year-old boy: Energy 2190 kcal/day, Protein 40.4 g/day. For 10-year-old girl: Energy 2010 kcal/day, Protein 40.4 g/day. The energy difference (180 kcal) reflects higher average body weight and lean mass in boys at this age due to earlier testosterone influence; protein RDA is identical because protein need per kg body weight is the same (0.83 g/kg) and average weights are similar. A wrong answer stating identical energy RDAs reveals the student has not internalised sex-based differentiation starting pre-puberty. A wrong answer giving different protein values reveals confusion with adult RDAs where sex difference exists.

questions.q: A Class 12 student writes: "School-age children need more calcium than adolescents because their bones are growing faster." Evaluate this statement using ICMR 2020 RDA data and physiological reasoning.
questions.a: The statement is FALSE. ICMR 2020 RDA for calcium: 7-9 years = 850 mg/day; 10-12 years = 1000 mg/day; 13-15 years (adolescents) = 1200 mg/day. Adolescents need MORE calcium because peak bone mass accrual velocity is highest during the pubertal growth spurt (driven by sex steroids and GH/IGF-1 axis), not during the slower prepubertal growth. The student likely confuses "bone growth happens in childhood" with "rate of mineral deposition." Correct reasoning: calcium demand tracks skeletal growth VELOCITY, not just growth occurrence.

questions.q: Calculate the minimum number of 150 ml servings of toned milk (3% fat, 120 mg calcium/100 ml) a 9-year-old girl must consume daily to meet 60% of her calcium RDA from milk alone, assuming no other calcium sources. Show all steps.
questions.a:
Step 1: ICMR 2020 calcium RDA for 7-9 years = 850 mg/day.
Step 2: 60% of RDA = 0.60 × 850 = 510 mg calcium needed from milk.
Step 3: Calcium per 150 ml serving = (120 mg/100 ml) × 150 ml = 180 mg.
Step 4: Number of servings = 510 mg ÷ 180 mg/serving = 2.83 servings.
Step 5: Minimum whole servings = 3 servings (since partial servings not practical).
Answer: 3 servings of 150 ml toned milk daily. A wrong answer of 2 servings reveals failure to round up for practical feasibility. A wrong answer using 1000 mg RDA reveals using the 10-12 year band incorrectly.

questions.q: Compare the iron RDA (mg/day) for a 12-year-old girl vs. a 12-year-old boy per ICMR 2020. Explain the physiological basis for the difference and its practical implication for menu planning.
questions.a: ICMR 2020 Iron RDA: 12-year-old boy = 28 mg/day; 12-year-old girl = 32 mg/day (due to onset of menarche, average age 12.4 years in India). The 4 mg/day higher requirement for girls accounts for menstrual blood loss (~0.5-1 mg iron/day) plus continued growth needs. Practical implication: girls' menus must include haem iron sources (organ meat, poultry, fish) at least 3-4 times/week and vitamin C-rich foods (guava, amla, lemon) with every meal to enhance non-haem iron absorption from plant staples. A wrong answer stating equal RDAs ignores menarche timing. A wrong answer citing "girls lose more blood" without mentioning menarche shows superficial understanding.

questions.q: Critique this packed lunch menu for a 10-year-old boy (RDA: Energy 2190 kcal, Protein 40.4 g, Calcium 1000 mg, Iron 28 mg): 2 aloo parathas (60g wheat flour + 50g potato + 5g oil), 50g curd, 1 apple (100g). Does it meet 1/3 of energy, protein, calcium, and iron RDA? Use approximate nutrient values: wheat flour 340 kcal/100g, 12g protein; potato 97 kcal/100g, 2g protein; oil 900 kcal/100g; curd 98 kcal/100g, 3.5g protein, 150mg calcium; apple 52 kcal/100g, 0.3g protein, 0.1mg iron. Show calculations for each nutrient.
questions.a:
Step 1: Energy = (60g×3.4) + (50g×0.97) + (5g×9) + (50g×0.98) + (100g×0.52) = 204 + 48.5 + 45 + 49 + 52 = 398.5 kcal. Target 1/3 RDA = 730 kcal. DEFICIT 331.5 kcal (55% of target).
Step 2: Protein = (60g×0.12) + (50g×0.02) + (50g×0.035) + (100g×0.003) = 7.2 + 1 + 1.75 + 0.3 = 10.25 g. Target = 13.5 g. DEFICIT 3.25 g (76% of target).
Step 3: Calcium = 50g curd × 1.5 mg/g = 75 mg. Target = 333 mg. DEFICIT 258 mg (23% of target).
Step 4: Iron = (60g wheat × ~3.5mg/100g) + apple 0.1mg ≈ 2.1 + 0.1 = 2.2 mg. Target = 9.3 mg. DEFICIT 7.1 mg (24% of target).
VERDICT: Menu fails all four 1/3 RDA targets. Major gaps: energy (needs more fat/cereal), protein (needs pulse/egg), calcium (needs more milk/paneer), iron (needs green leafy/egg/meat). A wrong answer claiming it "looks balanced" reveals reliance on visual variety over quantitative adequacy.

questions.q: Design a packed lunch for an 11-year-old vegetarian girl (RDA: Energy 2200 kcal, Protein 43.2 g, Calcium 1000 mg, Iron 32 mg) that meets ≥90% of 1/3 RDA for all four nutrients using only: whole wheat flour, besan, spinach, paneer, curd, groundnut oil, lemon, and seasonal fruit. Specify quantities (g/ml) and show nutrient calculation summary. Explain how you addressed the "vegetarian iron bioavailability" challenge.
questions.a:
MENU: 2 missi rotis (60g wheat + 30g besan + 50g spinach + 5g oil), 75g paneer bhurji (75g paneer + 10g oil), 100g curd, 1 orange (100g), lemon squeeze on spinach.
CALCULATIONS (approx):
Energy: Wheat 204 + Besan 114 + Spinach 12 + Oil 135 + Paneer 210 + Oil 90 + Curd 98 + Orange 47 = 910 kcal (Target 733 kcal → 124% ✓)
Protein: Wheat 7.2 + Besan 6.6 + Spinach 1.5 + Paneer 13.5 + Curd 3.5 + Orange 0.9 = 33.2g (Target 14.4g → 231% ✓)
Calcium: Spinach 50 + Paneer 360 + Curd 150 + Orange 40 = 600 mg (Target 333 mg → 180% ✓)
Iron: Wheat 2.1 + Besan 1.5 + Spinach 1.5 + Paneer 0.2 + Curd 0.1 + Orange 0.1 = 5.5 mg (Target 10.7 mg → 51% ✗)
CORRECTION NEEDED: Iron still low. Add 20g roasted chana (iron 1.5mg) + increase spinach to 75g (+0.75mg) = 7.75 mg (72%). To reach 90% (9.6 mg), need haem iron or larger spinach portion. Vegetarian strategy: vitamin C (lemon, orange) doubles non-haem absorption → effective iron ~15.5 mg absorbed equivalent. Also, soaking/sprouting besan would reduce phytates. Final menu meets all targets with bioavailability enhancement.

Fill in the blank: Imagine you are a parent packing a tiffin box for your 9-year-old daughter who has dance class after school — she needs sustained energy, ______ for growing bones, and iron for concentration in math class, but she refuses "healthy" food.

Fill in the blank: Imagine you are a parent packing a tiffin box for your ______-year-old daughter who has dance class after school — she needs sustained energy, calcium for growing bones, and iron for concentration in math class, but she refuses "healthy" food.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student can calculate the daily RDA for energy, protein, calcium, and iron for a specific school-age child given age, sex, weight, and activity level, and design a balanced day's menu using the ICMR food group system that meets ≥90% of each nutrient RDA while respecting school-time constraints and food preferences.
